title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 国家公民 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）
meta: 主题语境：国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）　|　核心词汇：minister　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 minister 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1985 the clerk ① named the minister that no applicant in the office would have recorded, and he said the naming was the whole of the month. The ② minister, meaning the official itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed unrecorded in the book; a minister, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ minister in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ minister at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A minister, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the clerk said the recording is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the minister was the whole of the matter, meaning the duty and not the official. The ⑥ minister, meaning the duty and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; minister, he said, is either something you name or the only word that means both an official and a duty. He said the duty is the part they remember.

By 1990 the ⑦ minister had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ minister of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of recording; minister, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ minister I remember is the official recorded in the file, which closed in 1992 and is still recorded as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ minister, my mother said in 1994, is the only official that improves by being recorded; every minister, she said, is a duty that has agreed to look like an official. She said the duty was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 部长；大臣（指办事处里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 部长；大臣（指那位部长本身，与小小的印章相对）
C. 固定搭配：name the minister 任命这一位部长
D. n. 部长；大臣（指留给孩子们签的那一份）
E. n. 部长之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的部长之事）
F. n. 部长；大臣（指卷宗里写到、被记载的那一位）
G. n. 部长、职责（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 职责（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: named the minister that no applicant in the office would have recorded
The minister, meaning the official itself and not the stamp
the minister at the far counter
the minister was the whole of the matter

The minister of the whole thing
A minister, my mother said in 1994

answers.why: name the minister 意为“任命这一位部长”，1985 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯记载的一位部长做了一遍。
minister 意为“部长；大臣”，指那位部长本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被记载。
minister 意为“部长；大臣”，指办事处里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
minister 意为“部长；大臣”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
minister 意为“部长、职责”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这位职责就是那件事的全部。
minister 意为“职责”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位部长，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
minister 意为“部长；大臣”，指卷宗里写到、被记载的那一位，到 1990 年这一位成了卷宗里的一行。
minister 意为“部长之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的部长之事是一处办事处和三个月份的记载。
minister 意为“部长；大臣”，我记得的是卷宗里记载过的那一位，1992 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一位。
minister 为抽象总称，母亲 1994 年说，部长是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的部长。
